title: Fluffy Couscous with Olive Oil and Parsley
summary: Instant couscous toasted golden in olive oil, steamed off the heat for 7 min and forked loose with parsley.

ingredients.note: use water for a lower-salt result; shop-bought stock may contain celery, so check the label

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
flat-leaf parsley, chopped, plus a sprig to serve

steps.title: Toast the grains
steps.text: Warm 1 tbsp of the oil in the saucepan over medium-high heat, tip in the couscous and stir for 3-5 min. Once the grains look lightly golden and smell nutty, they are ready; toasting adds flavour and helps keep each grain separate.

steps.title: Add boiling liquid
steps.text: Pour in the 400 ml boiling water or stock with the salt, give it a single stir, then clamp on the lid and lift the pan off the heat. Leave it alone for 7 min so the couscous can soak up every drop of steam.

steps.title: Fluff thoroughly
steps.text: Lift the lid and spend a full minute raking through the couscous with a fork. Breaking every clump now gives the light, sandy texture you want.

steps.title: Season and serve
steps.text: Fork through the rest of the oil, the parsley and the pepper. Heap it in a bowl, crown it with a parsley sprig and serve warm.

tips: Stirring the couscous while it steams makes it gummy; leave the lid on and let it be.
Use water rather than stock if you are watching salt.
Too much liquid is the usual cause of soggy couscous; measure the 400 ml exactly.
Add lemon zest or toasted nuts for variety.
storage: Cool quickly and refrigerate covered up to 3 days. Eat cold as a salad or reheat with a splash of water, covered, until piping hot (74 °C), fluffing again with a fork. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
